correctness.rationale: For any full-covered five-point support, translate its full-witness radius-two center to zero. Then all rows have weight <=2 and their nonzero coordinate columns are nonzero 5-bit masks with multiplicity at most two, with each row degree <=2. Every possible such template is enumerated exactly (14,778 templates, 7,260 with distinct rows). For a center of weight >=5 no row lies in its radius-two ball, and every other trace is produced by a center supported on at most four active or auxiliary-zero coordinates. Enumerating all such centers yields a universal maximum of 27 traces and no five-point shattered support; a Q6 witness attains 27. The independently derived small-dimension arguments yield VC dimensions 0,0,1,3,4 for dimensions 1,2,3,4,>=5, with an explicit four-point witness from dimension five. All critical integer computations are replayable using the embedded checker; it is a finite exhaustive proof after the dimension-independent reduction, not a finite-dimensional experiment.

value.rationale: This identifies an exact natural learning-theoretic invariant for the family of all fixed-radius-two Hamming balls over arbitrarily large binary cubes: the sharp local trace maximum is 27 of 32 on five points and the VC dimension stabilizes at four, first occurring at dimension five. The 27-trace extremum goes beyond the dimension-only obstruction, and the finite-template reduction gives a bounded, inspectable explanation for an unrestricted ambient-dimension result. These bounds are not numerical consequences of the earlier distance-one open-neighborhood theorem.
